answer: A vote needs its own clock. Each seat signs twenty time-stamped nonces at minutes the seed picks, and the ledger fits the offsets into a skew curve in parts per million. Two seats whose curves track within three ppm share one quartz crystal, so they fold into a single vote and forfeit 30,000 POA apiece; virtual machines inherit the host's drift and collapse together. NTP fixes the offset, not the drift shape. A board costs $45, a cloud clone pennies, so a thousand real seats run $45,000 before power. A lotus opens from mud at the pond's nadir, not from the surface it floats on.
